answer_text:
Let

\[
f(k)=k^{19}-k
\]

and let

\[
D=\gcd\{f(k):1<k<20,\ k\in\mathbb N\}=\gcd\{f(2),f(3),\dots,f(19)\}.
\]

Since \(k=2\) is included,

\[
D\mid f(2)=2^{19}-2.
\]

Factor:

\[
2^{19}-2=2(2^{18}-1)=2(2^9-1)(2^9+1).
\]

Now

\[
2^9-1=511=7\cdot 73,
\]

and

\[
2^9+1=513=27\cdot 19=3^3\cdot 19.
\]

Thus

\[
2^{19}-2=2\cdot 3^3\cdot 7\cdot 19\cdot 73.
\]

So any prime factor of \(D\) must be one of

\[
2,3,7,19,73,
\]

with exponents bounded by those above.

Now show that \(2,3,7,19\) all divide every \(f(k)\).

For \(p\in\{2,3,7,19\}\), we have \(p-1\mid 18\). Hence for any integer \(k\),

- if \(p\mid k\), then clearly \(p\mid k^{19}-k\);
- if \(p\nmid k\), Fermat’s little theorem gives \(k^{p-1}\equiv 1\pmod p\), and since \(19=1+m(p-1)\),

\[
k^{19}=k(k^{p-1})^m\equiv k\pmod p.
\]

Therefore

\[
2\cdot 3\cdot 7\cdot 19=798
\]

divides every element of \(A\), so

\[
798\mid D.
\]

It remains to rule out any extra factors from

\[
2^{19}-2=798\cdot 9\cdot 73.
\]

So write \(D=798q\), where

\[
q\mid 9\cdot 73.
\]

Check \(k=3\).

Modulo \(9\),

\[
f(3)=3^{19}-3\equiv 0-3\equiv 6\pmod 9,
\]

so \(9\nmid f(3)\). Hence \(3\nmid q\).

Modulo \(73\),

\[
3^6=729\equiv -1\pmod{73},
\]

so

\[
3^{18}\equiv -1\pmod{73}.
\]

Then

\[
f(3)=3^{19}-3=3\cdot 3^{18}-3\equiv 3(-1)-3\equiv -6\not\equiv 0\pmod{73}.
\]

Thus \(73\nmid f(3)\), so \(73\nmid q\).

Since \(q\mid 9\cdot 73\) but is divisible by neither \(3\) nor \(73\), we get \(q=1\). Therefore

\[
D=798.
\]

\[
\boxed{798}
\]
